job.style: a news-style report about a real-world situation

passage: In the diverse nation of Republica, the government recently faced a constitutional debate regarding the distribution of authority. To ensure stability, the constitution mandates that the legislature, executive, and judiciary operate independently, each holding specific powers to check the others. This horizontal arrangement prevents any single organ from dominating the state. Furthermore, the constitution clearly defines the jurisdiction of the national and regional governments. The Union List contains subjects of national importance, while the State List includes matters of local concern, ensuring that the central government cannot unilaterally legislate on regional affairs. Recently, the government introduced a third tier of administration, granting significant autonomy to village councils. This decentralisation does not strip the state government of its authority; instead, it empowers local bodies to manage grassroots issues while the state maintains its constitutional responsibilities. Finally, the national policy explicitly protects the rights of minority groups, ensuring that the majority community cannot impose its will on others. This approach reflects the moral necessity of power sharing, where every citizen's voice is respected regardless of their numerical strength in the population.

items.evidence: To ensure stability, the constitution mandates that the legislature, executive, and judiciary operate independently, each holding specific powers to check the others.
items.q: Why does Republica let the legislature, executive and judiciary hold separate powers?
options: So no single organ can dominate the others
So the state is split into central and regional levels
So the majority community can decide every matter
So the legislature can make laws on every subject
items.explain: Each organ checks the others, which prevents any single organ from dominating the state.

wrong.why: confuses horizontal sharing with levels of government
thinks democracy means majority decides everything
thinks lawmakers can legislate on any subject

items.evidence: The Union List contains subjects of national importance, while the State List includes matters of local concern, ensuring that the central government cannot unilaterally legislate on regional affairs.
items.q: Republica's central government wants a law on a purely local matter. What can it do?
options: It cannot pass the law on its own
It can pass it by adding it to the Union List
It can pass it since it is the national government
It can pass it if the villages agree
items.explain: The constitution lists regional matters under the State List, so the centre cannot legislate on them alone.

wrong.why: thinks the Union List can absorb any subject
thinks the Centre can make laws on any subject
thinks village approval gives the centre power

items.evidence: This decentralisation does not strip the state government of its authority; instead, it empowers local bodies to manage grassroots issues while the state maintains its constitutional responsibilities.
items.q: Village councils now have more autonomy. What does this mean for the state government?
options: It keeps its own constitutional duties
It hands all its power to the councils
It must now follow the national government
It loses its place as a tier of government
items.explain: Decentralisation empowers local bodies, but the state still keeps its constitutional responsibilities and authority.

wrong.why: thinks the state loses all power to local bodies
mixes up vertical sharing with central control
thinks a new tier removes an older one

items.evidence: This approach reflects the moral necessity of power sharing, where every citizen's voice is respected regardless of their numerical strength in the population.
items.q: Besides keeping peace, why is power sharing considered valuable in Republica?
options: It respects every citizen's voice, however few they are
It lets the largest group lead without limits
It gives each region the same number of laws
It makes only the village councils powerful
items.explain: Power sharing respects every citizen's voice whatever their numbers, so it has moral value beyond reducing conflict.

wrong.why: thinks the majority should decide everything
thinks sharing power is only about quieting conflict
thinks sharing means equal splitting of laws
